title: SQL Injection 101
description:
A basic login form is vulnerable to SQL injection. Can you bypass the authentication?

The login page accepts username and password. Try to think like an attacker.
author: admin

title: Caesar's Revenge
description: Decrypt the following ciphertext: "Fdhvduflvhdvblqwkhiluvw". The key is 3. This is a classic substitution cipher.
author: admin

title: Hidden in Plain Sight
description:
Download the image and look closely. Sometimes the answer is hiding in the metadata or encoded in the pixels.
Extract the hidden message from the provided file.
author: admin

title: Buffer Overflow Basics
description:
A simple C program has a buffer overflow vulnerability. Read the source code and exploit it to print the flag.
The program reads 200 bytes into a 64-byte buffer.
author: admin

title: XSS Reflected
description:
A search page reflects user input without sanitization. Craft a payload that triggers a JavaScript alert.
Prove the vulnerability exists.
author: admin

title: Reverse the Binary
description:
A stripped binary needs to be reverse engineered. Find the correct password that makes the program print the flag.
Use a disassembler to analyze the executable.
author: admin

title: RSA Oracle
description:
An RSA encryption oracle gives you the encrypted flag. The public key is (n=3233, e=17). Find the private key and decrypt the message.
Hint: n is very small for this challenge.
author: admin

title: Command Injection
description:
A web application pings an IP address you provide. It doesn't sanitize the input properly. Can you execute arbitrary commands?
Try to read /etc/passwd or list the directory.
author: admin

title: Packet Detective
description:
A pcap file is provided containing network traffic. Find the flag hidden in the packets.
Look for unusual data in the TCP streams.
author: admin

title: Hash Collision
description:
Find two different inputs that produce the same MD5 hash starting with "0e". This is a PHP type juggling vulnerability.
The provided code uses loose comparison (==).
author: admin

title: Binary Exploitation 101
description:
A simple format string vulnerability exists in the binary. Use %x and %n to read and write memory.
Leak the stack cookie and bypass NX protection.
author: admin
